claims.source: In line with the biochemical differences noted for GST-EPS15 (1-314) engagement, both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with a GST-EPS15R (1-365) fusion, while the Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claims.claim: The Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not cross-react with GST-EPS15R (1-365).
claims.source: In line with the biochemical differences noted for GST-EPS15 (1-314) engagement, both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with a GST-EPS15R (1-365) fusion, while the Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Nb E_3 binding to EPS15R is comparatively weak.
claims.source: Nb E_3 binding to EPS15R is comparatively weak, however.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 is an orthosteric, function-blocking pseudoequivalent NPF ligand for the Eps15/R protein EH domains.
claims.source: In sum, the biochemical data indicate that Nb E_142 is an orthosteric, function-blocking pseudoequivalent NPF ligand for the Eps15/R protein EH domains.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the biochemical characterization data.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 does not interact appreciably with GST-intersectin 1 (1-312).
claims.source: Yet in the same binding assay, Nb E_142 does not interact appreciably with GST-intersectin 1 (1-312) although the unmistakable Nb binding to both GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) and GST-EPS15 (1–217/EH1 + 2) is apparent (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains.
claims.source: This indicates importantly that additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains, and likely accounts for the markedly higher apparent affinity of this Nb over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of binding to intersectin 1.

claims.claim: Additional non-NPF side chains likely account for the markedly higher apparent affinity of Nb E_142 over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
claims.source: This indicates importantly that additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains, and likely accounts for the markedly higher apparent affinity of this Nb over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
claims.evidence: This is an inference drawn from the binding data.

claims.claim: It is improbable that Nb E_142 binds to other proteins with C-terminal EH domains, like EHD1.
claims.source: Also, since none of the anti-EPS15 Nbs display acidic residues trailing the NPF in CDR3, it makes it improbable that Nb E_142 binds to other proteins with C-terminal EH domains, like EHD1 (Kieken et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on sequence analysis and knowledge of EHD1 binding requirements, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Using 2 μM Nb E_142 and immobilized GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) varied from 0.5 to 20 μM, saturation occurs at around 10 μM and half-maximal binding occurs at ~3 μM.
claims.source: Using 2 μM Nb E_142 and immobilized GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) varied from 0.5 to 20 μM, saturation occurs at around 10 μM and half-maximal binding occurs at ~3 μM (Figure 3C–D).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from titration assays, with reference to Figures 3C-D.

claims.claim: With the larger GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion, half-maximal binding is also seen at ~2 μM.
claims.source: With the larger GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion, half-maximal binding is also seen at ~2 μM (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from titration assays, with reference to Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) and GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion proteins.
claims.source: That the apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for the two fusion proteins indicates that binding to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the titration assay data.

claims.claim: Binding of Nb E_142 to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
claims.source: That the apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for the two fusion proteins indicates that binding to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the titration assay data.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength.
claims.source: Thus Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength; these results demonstrate that the KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the titration assay data, compared to established knowledge about NPF peptide affinity, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide.
claims.source: Thus Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength; these results demonstrate that the KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the titration assay data, compared to established knowledge about NPF peptide affinity, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 is an immunoprecipitation-grade reagent.
claims.source: Nb E_142 is an immunoprecipitation-grade reagent.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from immunoprecipitation experiments.

claims.claim: Purified His6-tagged Nb E_142 bound to Ni-NTA-agarose efficiently immunoprecipitates Eps15 from both K-562 erythroleukemia cell lysates and rat brain cytosol.
claims.source: In addition to the binary interaction with recombinant GST-EPS15 (1-314) antigen (Figure 3E), purified His6-tagged Nb E_142 bound to Ni-NTA-agarose efficiently immunoprecipitates Eps15 from both K-562 erythroleukemia cell (Lozzio and Lozzio, 1975) lysates and rat brain cytosol (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3E and a citation.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 recognizes the native full-length Eps15 protein.
claims.source: This Nb thus recognizes the native full-length protein.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claims.claim: Nb E_142 quantitatively precipitates EPS15R from K-562 lysate.
claims.source: And in agreement with Nb E_142 also interacting with EPS15R (Figure 3A), there is quantitative precipitation of EPS15R from the K-562 lysate.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claims.claim: FCHO1, FCHO2 and AP-2 (α subunits) co-immunoprecipitate with EPS15/R immobilized through the EH domain regions by Nb E_142.
claims.source: Analysis of co-immunoprecipitating components shows the known EPS15/R interaction partners FCHO1, FCHO2 and AP-2 (α subunits) (Figure 2B) are co-recovered with the EPS15/R immobilized through the EH domain regions by Nb E_142 (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figures 2B and 3E.

claims.claim: The extent of recovery of cytosolic FCHO1/2 and AP-2 mirrors the known differential affinities.
claims.source: The extent of recovery of cytosolic FCHO1/2, which bind to the C-terminal DPF region of EPS15/R with the μ-homology domain (μHD) (Henne et al., 2010; Reider et al., 2009; Umasankar et al., 2012), and AP-2, which binds to the DPF region of EPS15/R utilizing the appendages of the α and β2 subunits (Benmerah et al., 1996; Iannolo et al., 1997), mirrors the known differential affinities (Ma et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunoprecipitation data, supported by citations.

claims.claim: NPF-dependent EH domain binding partners (HRB) do not co-precipitate with Eps15/R in the presence of Nb E_142.
claims.source: In the same assay, NPF-dependent EH domain binding partners (HRB, Figure 3E) do not co-precipitate with Eps15/R, again in line with function-blocking Nb activity.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3E.

claims.claim: The diffuse, rather featureless intracellular distribution of an mNeonGreen (mNG)-tagged Nb E_142 fusion is not substantially different from the control mNG protein alone.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, when transiently transfected into HeLa cells, the diffuse, rather featureless intracellular distribution of an mNeonGreen (mNG)-tagged (Shaner et al., 2013) Nb E_142 fusion is not substantially different from the control mNG protein alone, and is clearly distinct from the punctate pattern of endogenous EPS15 staining in these cells detected with an anti-peptide antibody recognizing the extreme C-terminus (Hinrichsen et al., 2003) (Figure 4A–E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 4A-E and citations.

claims.claim: In fewer than half the transfected cells, small concentrations of mNG-Nb E_142 that overlap some EPS15 puncta are seen.
claims.source: In fewer than half the transfected cells, small concentrations of mNG-Nb E_142 that overlap some EPS15 puncta are seen (Figure 4B', arrowheads).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4B'.

claims.claim: In some mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells an alteration in the steady-state distribution of endogenous EPS15 is evident compared with the adjacent non-transfected cells.
claims.source: While superficially these results suggest Nb E_142 may not function effectively as a so-called chromobody (Rothbauer et al., 2006), in some mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells an alteration in the steady-state distribution of endogenous EPS15 is evident compared with the adjacent non-transfected cells (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4G and a citation.

claims.claim: The intensity of the EPS15 surface puncta is diminished in mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells relative to adjacent non-transfected cells, indicative of less EPS15 deposition at these sites.
claims.source: The intensity of the EPS15 surface puncta is diminished relative to adjacent non-transfected cells, indicative of less EPS15 deposition at these sites, and some limited interference with EPS15 function.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation and interpretation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments.

claims.claim: In adherent cell membrane cortices from inadvertently sheared-off cells, a dim mNG-Nb E_142 signal is seen to colocalize closely with endogenous EPS15.
claims.source: Additionally, in adherent cell membrane cortices from inadvertently sheared-off cells (identified by lack of DNA staining), a dim mNG-Nb E_142 signal is seen to colocalize closely with endogenous EPS15 (Figure 4B, arrows, and Figure 4C-E).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 4B-E.

claims.claim: In viable cells EPS15/R deposited at clathrin coat assembly sites at the plasma membrane have EH domains locally occupied in a way that makes Nb E_142 binding unfavorable.
claims.source: As Nb E_142 is able to robustly immunoprecipitate EPS15(R) from cytosol, and because the Nbs act as pseudoligands, these transfection data suggest that in viable cells EPS15/R deposited at clathrin coat assembly sites at the plasma membrane have EH domains locally occupied in a way that makes Nb E_142 binding unfavorable.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data, combined with the immunoprecipitation data.

claims.claim: A tandem mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 protein construct labels punctate AP-2-positive structures at very low expression levels in HeLa cells.
claims.source: The concept of avidity-dependent, regionalized NPF occupancy of the EPS15/R EH domains gathered at incipient clathrin-coated structures is supported experimentally by the intracellular distribution and positioning of a transiently transfected triple Nb E_142 array. In HeLa cells, compared with the single Nb E_142 fusion, a larger mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 protein construct (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) now labels punctate AP-2-positive structures at very low expression levels.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The increased efficiency of EPS15/R labeling by the polyvalent mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 reporter signifies better apparent affinity for the massed EH domains at the sites of clathrin-coat assembly.
claims.source: Given that both the ectopic mNG-Nb E_142 and the mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 proteins each contain only a single fluorescent mNG domain, the increased efficiency of EPS15/R labeling by the polyvalent reporter (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) must signify better apparent affinity for the massed EH domains at the sites of clathrin-coat assembly.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Through avidity-based phenomena, artificially but flexibly grouped NPF-harboring Nbs can compete in vivo with the deployment multiple NPF-motifs by endogenous EH domain partner proteins.
claims.source: This indicates that through avidity-based phenomena, artificially but flexibly grouped NPF-harboring Nbs can compete in vivo with the deployment multiple NPF-motifs by endogenous EH domain partner proteins.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claims.claim: Transient overexpression of the control GFP-FYVE2 alone results in an enlarged labeled endosome compartment in HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.source: In HeLa SS6 cells, transient overexpression of the control GFP-FYVE2 alone, which binds to the endosomal compartment phospholipid marker phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PtdIns3P) (Chen and De Camilli, 2005), results in an enlarged labeled endosome compartment (Figure 5B), but the subcellular distribution of EPS15 remains undisturbed at clathrin-coated structures on the cell surface.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 5B and a citation.

claims.claim: A C-terminal Nb E_142 extension to the GFP-FYVE2 chimera produces a dramatic alteration in steady-state EPS15 positioning.
claims.source: A C-terminal Nb E_142 extension to the GFP-FYVE2 chimera produces a dramatic alteration in steady-state EPS15 positioning; the protein now colocalizes extensively with the clustered GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 fusion protein on large swollen endosomes and near completely disarranges assembly of EPS15 at typical scattered puncta on the plasma membrane (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 5C.

claims.claim: A fundamental tenet of coat-assisted vesicle formation is the cycling of coat protomers between a membrane-attached, assembled pool and a cytosolic, reserve pool.
claims.source: To explain the markedly altered subcellular distribution of EPS15, note that a fundamental tenet of coat-assisted vesicle formation is the cycling of coat protomers between a membrane-attached, assembled pool and a cytosolic, reserve pool.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about coat protein dynamics.

claims.claim: EPS15 is deposited from a supply in the dispersed soluble pool.
claims.source: If EPS15 is one of the early arriving pioneers at a nascent bud, it is deposited from a supply in the dispersed soluble pool.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the concept of coat protein cycling.

claims.claim: EPS15 cycles between a membrane-assembled and a cytosolic pool.
claims.source: The population of EPS15 in the cytosolic fraction (Figure 3) (van Delft et al., 1997a) confirms that this coat protein too cycles between a membrane-assembled and a cytosolic pool.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3) and supported by a citation.

claims.claim: A concentrating/multivalency effect of densely tethered Nb E_142 upon a two-dimensional membrane surface markedly increases the capacity of the Nb to capture endogenous EPS15 at that site.
claims.source: Additionally, like the tandem mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 fusion, a concentrating/multivalency effect of densely tethered Nb E_142 upon a two-dimensional membrane surface markedly increases the capacity of the Nb to capture endogenous EPS15 at that site.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claims.claim: The endosome-bound Nb E_142 can lure EPS15 from the soluble pool, titrating out the available free EPS15 such that, over time, little is available for deposition at new clathrin bud sites.
claims.source: The endosome-bound Nb E_142 can thus lure EPS15 from the latter soluble pool, titrating out the available free EPS15 such that, over time, little is available for deposition at new clathrin bud sites.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claims.claim: Organelle-attached Nb E_142 disturbs the steady-state balance of endogenous EPS15(R) positioning within the cell.
claims.source: Thus organelle-attached Nb E_142 disturbs the steady-state balance of endogenous EPS15(R) positioning within the cell, and therefore does function as an intrabody.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claims.claim: A mitochondria-tethered Nb E_142 fusion produces near-quantitative intracellular redistribution of endogenous EPS15 in HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.source: Very similar near-quantitative intracellular redistribution of endogenous EPS15 in HeLa SS6 cells expressing this fusion protein, but not a control (with central FKBP12-rapamycin binding (FRB) domain instead of the Nb E_142 module), is evident (Figure 6A and B).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 6A and B.

claims.claim: EPS15 puncta disappear from the basal surface in cells expressing Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP.
claims.source: EPS15 puncta disappear from the basal surface, and in medial confocal optical sections, cells expressing the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP do not display assembled EPS15 puncta at the cell margins, as seen in the adjacent untransfected or Akap1-FRB-iRFP transfected cells (Figure 6B', arrows).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 6B'.

claims.claim: Unlike GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 expression, even in high level expression cells, the mitochondria relocalized EPS15 does not elicit prominent AP-2 reorganization.
claims.source: But unlike GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 expression, even in high level expression cells, the mitochondria relocalized EPS15 does not elicit prominent AP-2 reorganization, possibly reflecting the absence of a suitable source of phosphatidylinositol 4, 5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) support on the mitochondrial outer membrane and/or the lack of suitable cargo with appropriate sorting signals to bind to the AP-2 adaptor core (Jackson et al., 2010; Traub and Bonifacino, 2013) (Figure 6C–D').
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 6C-D' and citations.

claims.claim: Both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-producing HeLa cells internalize transferrin despite the conspicuous difference in EPS15 positioning within the Nb E_142-expressing cells.
claims.source: Functional studies show that both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-producing HeLa cells internalize transferrin despite the conspicuous difference in EPS15 positioning within the Nb E_142-expressing cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B'), as is seen with the GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142-producing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B' and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A small subpopulation of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells display strongly suppressed, but not halted, transferrin internalization.
claims.source: A small subpopulation of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells display strongly suppressed, but not halted, transferrin internalization.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claims.claim: The diminished transferrin uptake in a fraction of cells is not likely due to mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP restriction but more probably due to the known cell-cycle dependence of transferrin endocytosis and/or heterogeneity in relative internalization dependent upon local context and positioning of the cultured cells within the adherent population.
claims.source: Since a similar fraction (~15%) of the Akap1-FRB-iRFP fusion produces a similar phenotype, the diminished transferrin uptake is not likely due to mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP restriction but more probably due to the known cell-cycle dependence of transferrin endocytosis (Sager et al., 1984) and/or heterogeneity in relative internalization dependent upon local context and positioning of the cultured cells within the adherent population (Snijder et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transferrin uptake assay data, supported by citations.

claims.claim: In the presence of a normal complement of endocytic clathrin coat components, artificial spatial displacement of EPS15/R onto mitochondria does not severely disrupt short-term clathrin-mediated endocytosis in parental HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.source: Overall, in the presence of a normal complement of endocytic clathrin coat components, artificial spatial displacement of EPS15/R onto mitochondria does not severely disrupt short-term clathrin-mediated endocytosis in parental HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transferrin uptake assay data.

claims.claim: Eps15/R and Fcho1/2 function along the same pathway in a redundant manner.
claims.source: As Eps15/R and Fcho1/2 function along the same pathway in a redundant manner (Ma et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016b), the effect of forced expression of the mitochondria-targeted Nb E_142 was explored in novel HeLa cells rendered FCHO1/2- and EPS15R-null by successive TALEN-mediated gene editing (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references, used to motivate the experimental approach, with reference to Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Three new triple-null lines were obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19.
claims.source: Of the three new triple-null lines obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19 (Figure 7B), and have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots (Figure 7C), one, clone #40, was selected for further analysis.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from TALEN-mediated gene editing, with reference to Figures 7B and 7C.

claims.claim: The three new triple-null lines have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots.
claims.source: Of the three new triple-null lines obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19 (Figure 7B), and have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots (Figure 7C), one, clone #40, was selected for further analysis.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoblotting, with reference to Figure 7C.

claims.claim: The relative cellular abundance of EPS15, AP-2 and several other clathrin-mediated endocytosis components is not changed in the HeLa clone #40 cells.
claims.source: The relative cellular abundance of EPS15, AP-2 and several other clathrin-mediated endocytosis components is not changed in the HeLa clone #40 cells (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoblotting, with reference to Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state.
claims.source: Like the HeLa clone #64/1.E cells from which they are derived, clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state (Figure 7D–F); compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunofluorescence microscopy, with reference to Figures 7D-F.

claims.claim: Compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
claims.source: Like the HeLa clone #64/1.E cells from which they are derived, clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state (Figure 7D–F); compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunofluorescence microscopy.

claims.claim: The abnormal distribution and morphology of clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited cells implies FCHO1/2 and EPS15R play some significant role in bud site selection and maintenance.
claims.source: This abnormal distribution and morphology of clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited cells implies FCHO1/2 and EPS15R play some significant role in bud site selection and maintenance.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunofluorescence microscopy data.

claims.claim: Both the HeLa #64/1.E and the clone #40 cells display defective clathrin-mediated endocytosis compared with parental HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.source: Side-by-side comparison of transferrin uptake and the steady-state abundance of transferrin receptors at the cell surface reveals that both the HeLa #64/1.E (Umasankar et al., 2014) and the clone #40 cells display defective clathrin-mediated endocytosis compared with parental HeLa SS6 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claims.claim: Fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (LAMP1-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C.
claims.source: Although fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein 1 (LAMP1)-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C (accounting for their long-term viability), the extent is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claims.claim: The extent of transferrin internalization in genome-edited cells is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.source: Although fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein 1 (LAMP1)-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C (accounting for their long-term viability), the extent is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claims.claim: The majority of the transferrin is bound to transferrin receptors diffusely situated over the plasma membrane in genome-edited cells.
claims.source: Instead, the majority of the transferrin is bound to transferrin receptors diffusely situated over the plasma membrane (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B' and C').
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1B' and C'.

claims.claim: The data indicate slowed egress of the transferrin receptor from the surface of the genome-edited cells for reentry into the endosomal compartment, leading to stalling and accumulation of this (and other) endocytic cargo at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Comparative accumulation of surface transferrin receptors in the genome-edited lines is confirmed by fluorescent transferrin labeling experiments conducted on ice for 60 min (unpublished); the data thus indicate slowed egress of the transferrin receptor from the surface of the genome-edited cells for reentry into the endosomal compartment, leading to stalling and accumulation of this (and other) endocytic cargo at the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the transferrin uptake assay data.

claims.claim: Transient expression of negative control Akap1-FRB-iRFP in the HeLa clone #40 cells has no obvious effect on the subcellular patterning of EPS15.
claims.source: Transient expression of negative control Akap1-FRB-iRFP in the HeLa clone #40 cells has no obvious effect on the subcellular patterning of EPS15 (Figure 8A), as in parental the HeLa SS6 cells.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 8A.

claims.claim: In Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP producing clone #40 cells, ectopic trapping of EPS15 on the mitochondria-massed Nb E_142 is clear, with a concomitant loss of EPS15 from the plasma membrane.
claims.source: By contrast, in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP producing clone #40 cells, ectopic trapping of EPS15 on the mitochondria-massed Nb E_142 is clear, with a concomitant loss of EPS15 from the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments.

claims.claim: In transfected clone #40 cells, AP-2 clusters at the surface are diminished in size and number in a manner that correlates with the efficiency of EPS15 segregation at mitochondria.
claims.source: In these transfected clone #40 cells, AP-2 clusters at the surface are diminished in size and number in a manner that correlates with the efficiency of EPS15 segregation at mitochondria (Figure 8B-F).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8B-F.

claims.claim: The majority of AP-2-positive puncta that do remain are populated with detectable endogenous EPS15 protein.
claims.source: The majority of AP-2-positive puncta that do remain are populated with detectable endogenous EPS15 protein (Figure 8C–F).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8C-F.

claims.claim: In the genetic background of clone #40 cells, stable membrane-associated AP-2 assemblies depend heavily on EPS15 for their generation.
claims.source: Thus, in this genetic background stable membrane-associated AP-2 assemblies depend heavily on EPS15 for their generation.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data in clone #40 cells.

claims.claim: Based on the apparent affinity and computed cellular abundance in HeLa cells, HRB, HRB-like protein (HRBL) and DAB2 are most likely the predominant interaction partners for the EH domains at assembling clathrin-coated structures.
claims.source: Based on the apparent affinity and computed cellular abundance in HeLa cells (Hein et al., 2015; Itzhak et al., 2016), HRB, HRB-like protein (HRBL) and DAB2 are most likely the predominant interaction partners for the EH domains at assembling clathrin-coated structures (Figure 2).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on affinity data and cellular abundance data from cited references, with reference to Figure 2.

claims.claim: In untransfected clone #40 cells, both EPS15 and HRB overlap at the aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures.
claims.source: Comparison of the steady-state distribution of EPS15 and HRB in clone #40 cells shows that whereas both proteins overlap at the aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures that are a distinctive feature of untransfected cells, in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells, neither protein is efficiently deposited on the plasma membrane (Figure 8G–L).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8G-L.

claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8G-L.

claims.claim: Ectopic GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) can reconstitute the regularly dispersed HeLa clathrin-coated structure pattern at very low levels of expression of the linker.
claims.source: Fully concordant with the widely dispersed PtdIns(4,5)P2 within the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane in both Akap1-FRB-iRFP- and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells is the restoration of extensive and apparently random deposition of AP-2 on co-transfection with GFP-tagged FCHO1 (1–609) (Figure 11). This truncated FCHO1 protein contains the membrane-binding N-terminal EFC/F-BAR domain (Umasankar et al., 2012; Henne et al., 2007) and the adjoining intrinsically disordered linker that appears to operate as an allosteric activator (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014), driving a reconfiguration of AP-2 from the closed to the membrane-bound open state (Jackson et al., 2010). Ectopic GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) can reconstitute the regularly dispersed HeLa clathrin-coated structure pattern at very low levels of expression of the linker (Figure 11A).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 11A and citations.

claims.claim: Measurement of AP-2-positive puncta in FCHO1 linker-expressing cells, compared with adjacent non-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells, documents the overall shift to smaller, more numerous 0.2–0.6 μm2 structures.

claims.claim: EPS15 is sequestered prominently by the overexpressed Nb decoy on mitochondria, and little endogenous EPS15 is deposited along with the corrected AP-2 in the compact, scattered surface puncta.

claims.claim: These striking results verify that FCHO1/2 act epistatically to EPS15/R.

claims.claim: A major role of EPS15/R is normally to cooperate with full-length FCHO1/2 to bind to and activate AP-2 proteins at incipient clathrin-coated structures.

claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: In depth characterization of the anti-EPS15 Nb E_142 shows this VHH is a versatile reagent in that it functions both in in vitro biochemical assays and as an effective intrabody in the reducing environment of the cell cytosol.
claims.source: In depth characterization of the anti-EPS15 Nb E_142 shows this VHH is a versatile reagent in that it functions both in in vitro biochemical assays and as an effective intrabody in the reducing environment of the cell cytosol.

claims.claim: Using new NPF motif-harboring llama Nbs, it is demonstrated that during assembly the collective EH domains of EPS15 and EPS15R deposited at clathrin-coated structures appear poorly accessible.
claims.source: Here, using new NPF motif-harboring llama Nbs, it is demonstrated that during assembly the collective EH domains of EPS15 and EPS15R deposited at clathrin-coated structures appear poorly accessible; this provides an important clue to the occupancy of EH domains during lattice assembly and sorting in light of the known modest KD for a single NPF•EH domain interaction (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the cell-based data, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The minimal region of Ede1p necessary for proper targeting to clathrin-coated buds is EH3, a flanking proline-rich region and the coiled-coil domain.
claims.source: In the budding yeast S. cerevisiae, where Hs EPS15 can substitute for the orthologous Ede1p, the minimal region of Ede1p necessary for proper targeting to clathrin-coated buds is EH3, a flanking proline-rich region and the coiled-coil domain (Lu and Drubin, 2017).

claims.claim: EH domains play a critical role in placing Eps15 at the membrane bud site but highlights the cooperativity of the binding information hardwired into Eps15/R and their early-arriving binding partners.

claims.claim: In metazoa, early-arriving binding partners of Eps15/R include AP-2, Fcho1/2, Hrb, Dab2, epsin, and CALM.

claims.evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claims.source: These endocytic proteins display a densely wired interactome, and it seems likely they are responsible for high frequency occupancy of the EH domains at clathrin assembly sites.

claims.source: Like EPS15/R, HRB/L (also designated AGFG1/2) and DAB2 are both detected in proximity labeling mass spectrometry experiments as early, and thus edge positioned, components (Paek et al., 2017).

claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The results from the new triple-null clone #40 HeLa cells expressing a mitochondria-bound Nb E_142 illustrate that without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R, coated assemblies do not form stably and clathrin-mediated endocytosis falters.

claims.evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, with reference to Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Both CALM and HRB operate as vital SNARE retrieving sorting adaptors.
claims.source: Both CALM and HRB operate as vital SNARE retrieving sorting adaptors (Miller et al., 2011; Pryor et al., 2008).

claims.claim: The Nb-directed mislocalization of EPS15 in the HeLa clone #40 cells leads to bulk loss of clathrin-coated structures and diminished clathrin-based uptake.

claims.claim: The EH domain proteins intersectin 1 and intersectin 2 cannot sustain clathrin-mediated endocytosis without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R.
claims.source: That the Nb-directed mislocalization of EPS15 in the HeLa clone #40 cells leads to bulk loss of clathrin-coated structures and diminished clathrin-based uptake indicates that the EH domain proteins intersectin 1 and intersectin 2, which are both expressed in HeLa cells (Figure 4) (Itzhak et al., 2016), cannot sustain the process without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R.

claims.source: Nb E_142 does not bind physically to the intersectin 1 EH domains, and although hierarchical clustering, based on ultrastructural localization within clathrin-coated structures, places EPS15/R and intersectin in distinct branches (Sochacki et al., 2017), and the BioPlex 2.0 database (with HEK 293 cells) (Schweppe et al., 2018) does not score EPS15/R as intersectin 1 or -2 binding partners, the noted discrepancy could be due to intersectins binding physically to EPS15/R (Sengar et al., 1999) and so being concomitantly unavailable when massed at an inappropriate intracellular organelle, or due to lower cellular abundance.

claims.source: While it is possible that a priming FCHO1/2•EPS15/R nanocluster (Ma et al., 2016) operates downstream or alongside AP-2 colliding with the plasma membrane in a suitable orientation to engage PtdIns(4,5)P2 through the binding sites on the large α- and β2-subunit trunks (Jackson et al., 2010; Gaidarov et al., 1996), the fact that the intrinsically disordered linker in Fcho1/2 appears to act as a regulator of AP-2 switching from the closed to the open state (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014) suggests that these pioneers promote the stable association of AP-2 with the membrane.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The strongest evidence for the model that pioneers promote the stable association of AP-2 with the membrane is the unmistakable reconstitution of apparently normal AP-2 puncta in the presence of a membrane-tethered FCHO1 linker domain in clone #40 cells.
claims.source: The strongest evidence for this model is the unmistakable reconstitution of apparently normal AP-2 puncta in the presence of a membrane-tethered FCHO1 linker domain in clone #40 cells (Figure 11).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells, with reference to Figure 11.

claims.claim: Under normal circumstances at the edge of a de novo forming coat, membrane-attached FCHO1/2 interacts with incoming EPS15/R through the μHD, steering the AP-2-bound EPS15 to relay the heterotetramer to FCHO1/2 for local access to the activating linker.
claims.source: Under normal circumstances at the edge of a de novo forming coat, membrane-attached FCHO1/2 interacts with incoming EPS15/R through the μHD (Ma et al., 2016; Shimada et al., 2016), steering the AP-2-bound EPS15 to relay the heterotetramer to FCHO1/2 for local access to the activating linker.
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the data, supported by citations.

claims.claim: This concept is in line with EPS15/R being the highest affinity binding partner of the FCHO1/2 μHD.
claims.source: This concept is in line with EPS15/R being the highest affinity binding partner of the FCHO1/2 μHD (Umasankar et al., 2012; Shimada et al., 2016) and being the only proteins in the genome with the tandem DPFX2-3DPFX2-3DPF SLiMs necessary for optimal μHD engagement, both FCHO1/2 (Umasankar et al., 2012; Henne et al., 2007) and EPS15 (Wang et al., 2016b) binding to PtdIns(4,5)P2, and the interdomain linker of FCHO1/2 regulating AP-2 (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014) to rearrange the μ2 subunit to co-align PtdIns(4,5)P2, YXXØ and [DE]XXXL[LI] cargo binding interaction surfaces at the planar plasma membrane (Jackson et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: The data are also consistent with these rim-localized pioneers being able to drive deposition of new, open AP-2 into the interior of the incipient lattice.
claims.source: The data are also consistent with these rim-localized pioneers being able to drive deposition of new, open AP-2 into the interior of the incipient lattice.

claims.claim: Large, long-lived clathrin assemblies in human embryonic stem cell-derived fibroblasts correlate with elevated expression levels of AP-2.
claims.source: It has recently been demonstrated that large, long-lived clathrin assemblies in human embryonic stem cell-derived fibroblasts correlate with elevated expression levels of AP-2 (Dambournet et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claims.claim: Even with high soluble levels of AP-2 and PtdIns(4,5)P2, normally sized and distributed clathrin-coated structures on the plasma membrane require the activity of EPS15/R and FCHO1/2.
claims.source: Strikingly, while this may be mechanistically related to the abnormal clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited HeLa clone #64/1.E and clone #40 cells, due to an increase in the cytosolic AP-2 pool, the effect of EPS15 impoundment in clone #40 cells shown here indicates that even with high soluble levels of AP-2 and PtdIns(4,5)P2, normally sized and distributed clathrin-coated structures on the plasma membrane require the activity of EPS15/R and FCHO1/2.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claims.claim: Conditionally hematopoietic compartment compound-null Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- mice are anemic due to dysfunctional erythrocyte differentiation and maturation.
claims.source: It has also just been reported that conditionally hematopoietic compartment compound-null Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- mice are anemic due to dysfunctional erythrocyte differentiation and maturation (Milesi et al., 2019).

claims.claim: The Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- double knock-out mice display strikingly abnormal accumulation of the transferrin receptor on the surface of the defective circulating red blood cell population.
claims.source: Remarkably, although the transferrin receptor is the prototypical AP-2-dependent YXXØ-signal-harboring transmembrane receptor (Traub and Bonifacino, 2013; Collawn et al., 1990), the Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- double knock-out mice display strikingly abnormal accumulation of the transferrin receptor on the surface of the defective circulating red blood cell population (Milesi et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is information from a cited reference, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The dysregulation of the efficient internalization of the transferrin receptor in the erythrocyte precursor cells (reticulocytes) expressing normal AP-2 is reminiscent of the phenotype of HeLa clone #40 cells with Nb E_142-mediated sequestration of EPS15.
claims.source: This dysregulation of the efficient internalization of the transferrin receptor in the erythrocyte precursor cells (reticulocytes) expressing normal AP-2 is obviously reminiscent of the phenotype of HeLa clone #40 cells with Nb E_142-mediated sequestration of EPS15 shown here, and independently reiterates the upstream role of Eps15/R (and Fcho1/2) in the proper functioning of the AP-2 adaptor complex under normal conditions.
claims.evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to the mouse model data, supported by a citation.

results.result: A phage-based immune llama VHH library was generated against the EPS15 EH1-3 domains (residues 1-314), yielding seven ELISA-positive clones representing three discrete families. Sequence analysis revealed the EH domains are ~32% identical and 50% similar to one another, and EPS15 residues 1-314 are ~60% identical and 77% similar to EPS15R residues 1-365. Pull-down assays demonstrated that Nb E_3 binds preferentially to EH3, while Nb E_142 and E_180 bind to multiple EH domains with Nb E_142 showing the highest apparent affinity and interacting with EH1, EH1+2, EH1-3, and EH2+3.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C53 collectively describe the generation, characterization, and binding specificity of anti-EPS15 nanobodies. The sequence analysis (C33, C35, C36) and pull-down assay data (C42-C53) provide converging evidence for the binding properties of the three nanobody families, with appropriate experimental controls (GST alone) and multiple constructs tested.

results.result: All seven anti-EPS15 nanobody clones contain a remarkable immunodominant Asn-Pro-Phe (NPF) tripeptide within the CDR3 region, a feature not found in any other characterized VHH clone except for some anti-Tulip virus X nanobodies. Since the majority of EH domain partners use NPF short linear motifs to bind EH domains, this strongly suggests the newly selected nanobodies bind to the functional interaction surface of the EH domain. A previously described anti-EPS15 nanobody lacking the NPF motif does not bind native EPS15 efficiently.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C61 describe a key structural feature of the nanobodies and its functional implications. The sequence analysis (C54, C55, C56) combined with established knowledge about EH domain binding (C57) and comparison to a control nanobody (C59-C61) provide strong support for the interpretation that these nanobodies are NPF-mimicking pseudoligands.

results.result: Site-directed mutagenesis replacing NPF with APA in Nb E_142 completely eliminates binding to GST-EPS15 (1-314), demonstrating the critical role of the NPF motif. While individual NPF motifs typically bind EH domains weakly (KD >100 μM), cyclized NPF peptides bind with ~10-fold higher affinity due to conformational rigidity. The structural constraints of the nanobody immunoglobulin fold and CDR3 loop likely similarly increase apparent affinity, with contributions from CDR1 and CDR2 also probable.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C68 provide direct experimental evidence (mutagenesis, C62) and mechanistic interpretation based on established knowledge (C63-C65) for how the nanobodies achieve higher affinity than natural NPF peptides. The speculation about CDR1/CDR2 contributions (C66-C68) is appropriately qualified and reasonable given the data.

results.result: In biochemical pull-down assays, immobilized GST-EPS15 (1-314) interacts with several NPF-harboring cytosolic partners from HeLa cell lysate in a dose-dependent manner, with apparent affinity correlating roughly with the number of NPF motifs (HRB: 5, DAB2: 5, epsin 1: 3, CALM: 2). HRB is the most avid binding partner, while CALM shows only limited binding. Nb E_142 is function-blocking, as supplementing lysate with equimolar Nb E_142 causes substantial loss of DAB2 and epsin 1 binding, while a fivefold molar excess produces near complete obstruction of HRB, DAB2, and epsin 1 interactions.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C77 describe competition experiments demonstrating the function-blocking activity of Nb E_142. The dose-dependent effects (C76, C77) and correlation with NPF motif number (C70) provide strong evidence for the mechanism of action. The data are internally consistent and appropriately controlled.

results.result: A W57A substitution in the EPS15 EH1 domain, which disrupts the canonical NPF interaction surface, abolishes Nb E_142 binding to GST-EPS15 (1-109) but has only a modest effect on binding to the larger GST-EPS15 (1-314) fusion. These data clearly indicate that Nb E_142 engages EH domains as an NPF-mimicking pseudoligand that contacts a conserved interaction site upon the canonical EH domain.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 provide mutagenesis data targeting a conserved residue in the NPF binding site. The differential effect on EH1 alone versus EH1-3 (C78, C79) is consistent with Nb E_142 binding to multiple EH domains, and the conclusion (C80) is well-supported by the combined mutagenesis and competition data.

results.result: Both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with GST-EPS15R (1-365), while the Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) mutant does not, though Nb E_3 binding to EPS15R is comparatively weak. The biochemical data indicate that Nb E_142 is an orthosteric, function-blocking pseudoequivalent NPF ligand for the Eps15/R protein EH domains.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C84 demonstrate cross-reactivity with the paralogous EPS15R protein, consistent with the high sequence similarity between EPS15 and EPS15R EH domains. The NPF→APA mutant control (C82) strengthens the conclusion that Nb E_142 functions as an NPF pseudoligand (C84).

results.result: Nb E_142 does not interact appreciably with GST-intersectin 1 (1-312), indicating that additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to selective binding to EPS15/R EH domains, which likely accounts for the markedly higher apparent affinity over native NPF ligands. Since none of the anti-EPS15 nanobodies display acidic residues trailing the NPF in CDR3, it is improbable that Nb E_142 binds to other proteins with C-terminal EH domains like EHD1.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C88 demonstrate specificity of Nb E_142 for EPS15/R over intersectin 1, despite all containing EH domains. The inference about additional non-NPF contributions (C86, C87) is well-supported by the selectivity data, and the prediction about EHD1 (C88) is reasonable based on sequence analysis.

results.result: Biochemical titrations show that using 2 μM Nb E_142 and varying immobilized GST-EPS15 (1-109/EH1) from 0.5 to 20 μM, saturation occurs at ~10 μM with half-maximal binding at ~3 μM. With GST-EPS15 (1-314/EH1-3), half-maximal binding is also ~2 μM. The similar apparent KD for both constructs indicates that binding to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity. Thus, Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength, considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C94 provide quantitative binding data from titration experiments. The similar KD values for EH1 alone and EH1-3 (C91, C92) support independent binding to each domain. The comparison to natural NPF peptides (C93, C94) is appropriately supported by citations to established affinity values.

results.result: Purified His6-tagged Nb E_142 bound to Ni-NTA-agarose efficiently immunoprecipitates Eps15 from K-562 cell lysates and rat brain cytosol, recognizing the native full-length protein. EPS15R is also quantitatively precipitated from K-562 lysate. Known EPS15/R interaction partners FCHO1, FCHO2, and AP-2 co-immunoprecipitate with EPS15/R, with recovery mirroring known differential affinities, while NPF-dependent EH domain binding partners like HRB do not co-precipitate, consistent with function-blocking nanobody activity.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C101 demonstrate that Nb E_142 is an immunoprecipitation-grade reagent that recognizes native EPS15/R. The selective co-immunoprecipitation of non-NPF-dependent partners (FCHO1/2, AP-2) but not NPF-dependent partners (HRB) (C99-C101) provides strong evidence for the function-blocking mechanism.

results.result: When transiently transfected into HeLa cells, mNG-tagged Nb E_142 shows a diffuse intracellular distribution not substantially different from control mNG alone, distinct from the punctate pattern of endogenous EPS15. In fewer than half the transfected cells, small concentrations of mNG-Nb E_142 overlap some EPS15 puncta, and in some cells the intensity of EPS15 surface puncta is diminished. In adherent cell membrane cortices from sheared-off cells, dim mNG-Nb E_142 signal colocalizes with endogenous EPS15. These data suggest that in viable cells, EPS15/R deposited at clathrin coat assembly sites have EH domains locally occupied in a way that makes Nb E_142 binding unfavorable.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C107 describe the unexpected poor labeling of clathrin-coated structures by monomeric mNG-Nb E_142 in living cells, contrasting with efficient binding in vitro. The interpretation (C107) that EH domains are occupied by endogenous partners at clathrin-coated structures is well-supported by the combined in vitro and in vivo data.

results.result: A tandem mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 protein construct labels punctate AP-2-positive structures at very low expression levels in HeLa cells, unlike the single Nb E_142 fusion. Since both constructs contain only a single mNG domain, the increased efficiency of EPS15/R labeling by the polyvalent reporter must signify better apparent affinity for the massed EH domains at clathrin-coat assembly sites. This indicates that through avidity-based phenomena, artificially grouped NPF-harboring nanobodies can compete in vivo with endogenous EH domain partner proteins deploying multiple NPF motifs.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C110 provide strong evidence for avidity effects in EH domain binding. The comparison between monomeric and trimeric nanobody constructs (C108, C109) controls for fluorophore number and directly demonstrates the importance of multivalency, supporting the interpretation about avidity-based competition (C110).

results.result: Transient overexpression of control GFP-FYVE2 alone results in an enlarged endosome compartment but undisturbed EPS15 distribution at the cell surface. A C-terminal Nb E_142 extension to GFP-FYVE2 produces dramatic alteration in steady-state EPS15 positioning, with extensive colocalization on swollen endosomes and near complete disarrangement of EPS15 at plasma membrane puncta. This is explained by EPS15 cycling between membrane-assembled and cytosolic pools, with the endosome-bound Nb E_142 luring EPS15 from the soluble pool through concentrating/multivalency effects, titrating out available free EPS15 such that little is available for deposition at new clathrin bud sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C118 demonstrate successful intracellular sequestration of EPS15 using organelle-tethered nanobodies. The control (GFP-FYVE2 alone, C111) and experimental (GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142, C112) comparison is appropriate, and the mechanistic interpretation (C113-C118) based on coat protein cycling is well-reasoned and consistent with established principles.

results.result: A mitochondria-tethered Nb E_142 fusion produces near-quantitative intracellular redistribution of endogenous EPS15 in HeLa SS6 cells, with EPS15 puncta disappearing from the basal surface. Unlike GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 expression, the mitochondria-relocalized EPS15 does not elicit prominent AP-2 reorganization. Both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-producing cells internalize transferrin despite the conspicuous difference in EPS15 positioning, though a small subpopulation shows suppressed internalization likely due to cell-cycle dependence or population heterogeneity rather than mitochondrial dysfunction. Overall, artificial spatial displacement of EPS15/R onto mitochondria does not severely disrupt short-term clathrin-mediated endocytosis in parental HeLa SS6 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C119-C125 demonstrate that EPS15 sequestration on mitochondria in wild-type cells does not severely impair endocytosis. The appropriate controls (Akap1-FRB-iRFP, C119, C122) and functional assays (transferrin uptake, C122-C124) support the conclusion (C125). The interpretation of the small subpopulation with reduced uptake (C124) is reasonable and appropriately qualified.

results.result: Novel HeLa cells rendered FCHO1/2- and EPS15R-null by successive TALEN-mediated gene editing were generated (clone #40). Three new triple-null lines exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15L1 gene and have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots. The relative cellular abundance of EPS15, AP-2, and several other clathrin-mediated endocytosis components is not changed in clone #40 cells. However, these cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state, with fewer, larger, and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies on the ventral membrane compared to parental HeLa SS6 cells, implying FCHO1/2 and EPS15R play a significant role in bud site selection and maintenance.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C132 describe the generation and characterization of triple-null cells. The genetic validation (C127, C128), protein abundance analysis (C129), and morphological characterization (C130-C132) provide comprehensive evidence for the phenotype. The interpretation about bud site selection (C132) is appropriately qualified as an implication rather than a definitive conclusion.

results.result: Both HeLa #64/1.E and clone #40 cells display defective clathrin-mediated endocytosis compared with parental HeLa SS6 cells. Although fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes in a 5 min pulse at 37°C, the extent is less than in HeLa SS6 cells. Instead, the majority of transferrin is bound to transferrin receptors diffusely situated over the plasma membrane. The data indicate slowed egress of the transferrin receptor from the cell surface for reentry into the endosomal compartment, leading to stalling and accumulation of endocytic cargo at the plasma membrane.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C137 demonstrate functional defects in endocytosis in the genome-edited cells. The transferrin uptake assays (C134-C136) provide direct evidence for impaired internalization, and the interpretation about slowed receptor egress (C137) is well-supported by the observed accumulation of surface transferrin receptors.

results.result: Transient expression of control Akap1-FRB-iRFP in HeLa clone #40 cells has no obvious effect on EPS15 subcellular patterning. In contrast, Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP produces clear ectopic trapping of EPS15 on mitochondria with concomitant loss from the plasma membrane. In transfected clone #40 cells, AP-2 clusters at the surface are diminished in size and number in a manner correlating with the efficiency of EPS15 segregation at mitochondria, and the majority of remaining AP-2-positive puncta are populated with detectable endogenous EPS15. Thus, in this genetic background, stable membrane-associated AP-2 assemblies depend heavily on EPS15 for their generation.
results.evaluation: Claims C138-C142 demonstrate a critical role for EPS15 in AP-2 assembly in the absence of FCHO1/2 and EPS15R. The appropriate control (Akap1-FRB-iRFP, C138) and the correlation between EPS15 sequestration and AP-2 loss (C140) provide strong evidence for the conclusion (C142).

results.result: Based on apparent affinity and cellular abundance, HRB, HRBL, and DAB2 are most likely the predominant interaction partners for EH domains at assembling clathrin-coated structures. In untransfected clone #40 cells, both EPS15 and HRB overlap at aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures, but in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells, neither protein is efficiently deposited on the plasma membrane. EPS15 is lured onto mitochondria but HRB is not, and EPS15 is associated with the few HRB puncta evident at the plasma membrane. Thus, in the presence of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP, HRB is essentially displaced into the soluble cytosolic compartment. These findings recapitulate the effect of combined EPS15 and EPS15R RNAi in parental HeLa clone #64/1.E cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C143-C148 demonstrate that EPS15 sequestration leads to loss of HRB from clathrin-coated structures. The inference about predominant partners (C143) is appropriately based on affinity and abundance data. The observation that HRB is displaced to the cytosol (C145-C147) is consistent with the function-blocking activity of Nb E_142 and supports the model that EPS15 EH domains recruit HRB to clathrin-coated structures.

results.result: The defects in AP-2-containing clathrin-coated structures in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected clone #40 cells translate into clathrin-mediated endocytosis dysfunction. Loss of EPS15 from surface puncta by massing upon mitochondria has a strong inhibitory effect on transferrin uptake. The presence of small intracellular endosomes positive for fluorescent tracer is strongly decreased compared with neighboring untransfected cells, with quantitation showing the number of >0.2 μm² transferrin-positive intracellular structures in untransfected cells is roughly double that of the EPS15-sequestered cell population. This inhibited internalization with mitochondria-appropriated EPS15 implies that FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R facilitate AP-2-dependent clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C149-C153 demonstrate that EPS15 sequestration in the triple-null background severely impairs endocytosis. The quantitative analysis (C152) and appropriate controls (untransfected cells) provide strong evidence. The conclusion (C153) is well-supported by the combined structural and functional data in the genome-edited cells.

results.result: Ectopic expression of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP is unlikely to grossly perturb PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels based on proper plasma membrane deposition of endogenous AP-2 in transfected HeLa SS6 cells. Using the PLCδ1 PH domain as a biosensor, both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells show abundant plasma membrane PtdIns(4,5)P2 despite marked differences in EPS15 localization. These results reveal that despite plasma membrane PtdIns(4,5)P2, elevated surface transferrin receptor levels, and normal cellular AP-2 concentration, the absence of utilizable FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R pioneers in HeLa clone #40 cells is not compatible with widespread and stable AP-2 deposition at the cell surface and clathrin-coated structure assembly. The parallel decrease in AP-2 and HRB puncta supports the notion that EPS15/R EH domains play a key role in docking HRB at nascent coated buds.
results.evaluation: Claims C154-C158 demonstrate that the defects in AP-2 assembly are not due to PtdIns(4,5)P2 depletion. The PtdIns(4,5)P2 biosensor experiments (C156) provide direct evidence, and the conclusion (C157) is well-supported by the combined data showing that pioneers are required despite the presence of PtdIns(4,5)P2, AP-2, and cargo.

results.result: Ectopic GFP-FCHO1 (1-609), containing the membrane-binding EFC/F-BAR domain and intrinsically disordered linker, can reconstitute the regularly dispersed clathrin-coated structure pattern at very low expression levels in clone #40 cells. Measurement of AP-2-positive puncta documents an overall shift to smaller, more numerous 0.2-0.6 μm² structures. EPS15 is sequestered prominently by overexpressed Nb decoy on mitochondria, and little endogenous EPS15 is deposited with the corrected AP-2 in compact surface puncta. Thus, the normalizing effect of the FCHO1 linker is manifest largely in the absence of co-assembled EPS15. The FCHO1-corrected phenotype closely mirrors results in clone #64/1.E cells. These results verify that FCHO1/2 act epistatically to EPS15/R and demonstrate clearly that a major role of EPS15/R is normally to cooperate with full-length FCHO1/2 to bind to and activate AP-2 proteins at incipient clathrin-coated structures.
results.evaluation: Claims C159-C167 provide strong evidence for epistasis between FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R. The rescue of AP-2 assembly by FCHO1 linker alone in the absence of EPS15 (C159-C162) is a key result demonstrating that FCHO1/2 can function independently of EPS15/R. The conclusion about epistasis and the role of EPS15/R (C166, C167) is well-supported by the rescue experiments and consistent with previous findings.

results.result: The G-Nb E_142-E3 plasmid, containing Nb E_142 fused to the XIAP E3 ligase RING domain, is highly effective in promoting degradation of EPS15 in transiently transfected cells positive for GFP, while the negative control parental GFE3 has negligible impact on EPS15 distribution. Effective elimination of EPS15/R by the tailored G-Nb E_142-E3 fusion protein still leaves AP-2 assembled at clathrin-coated sites on the plasma membrane of HeLa SS6 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C168-C169 demonstrate an alternative approach to EPS15 depletion using targeted degradation. The appropriate control (GFE3 without Nb E_142) and the observation that AP-2 remains at clathrin-coated sites despite EPS15 depletion (C169) are consistent with the sequestration experiments and support the conclusion that EPS15 is not absolutely required for AP-2 localization in wild-type cells.

results.result: In-depth characterization of anti-EPS15 Nb E_142 shows this VHH is a versatile reagent functioning both in in vitro biochemical assays and as an effective intrabody in the reducing environment of the cell cytosol. Using new NPF motif-harboring llama nanobodies, it is demonstrated that during assembly the collective EH domains of EPS15 and EPS15R deposited at clathrin-coated structures appear poorly accessible, providing an important clue to EH domain occupancy during lattice assembly and sorting in light of the known modest KD for a single NPF•EH domain interaction.
results.evaluation: Claims C170-C171 provide a summary of the key findings about the nanobody tool and its application to understanding EH domain occupancy. The conclusion about poor accessibility of EH domains at clathrin-coated structures (C171) is well-supported by the combined in vitro and in vivo data throughout the manuscript.

results.result: Clathrin coat inception depends on early-arriving proteins including Fcho1/2 and Eps15/R. Previous work using genome-edited cells described the role of the unstructured Fcho linker in stable AP-2 membrane deposition. The current study, expanding this strategy with new llama nanobodies against EPS15, shows an FCHO1/2-EPS15/R partnership plays a decisive role in coat initiation. A nanobody containing an Asn-Pro-Phe peptide within the CDR3 loop is a function-blocking pseudoligand for tandem EPS15/R EH domains. In living cells, EH domains at clathrin-coated structures are poorly accessible, indicating occupancy by endogenous NPF-bearing partners. Forcibly sequestering cytosolic EPS15 in genome-edited cells with nanobodies tethered to organelles has strong effects on clathrin coat structure and function by dictating the stability of AP-2 assemblies at the plasma membrane.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C8 summarize the main findings of the study as presented in the abstract. These claims are well-supported by the detailed experimental data presented throughout the manuscript, including nanobody characterization, sequestration experiments, and functional assays in genome-edited cells.

results.result: The introduction provides established background knowledge about clathrin-mediated endocytosis, including its evolutionary conservation, the ordered deposition of coat components, the role of pioneer proteins (Eps15, AP-2, Fcho1/2), and the extensive protein-protein interaction network of Eps15. Eps15 is a fibrous protein oligomer that localizes to the vast majority of cell surface clathrin-coated structures, is positioned predominantly at the margins of assembling lattices, and binds physically to numerous coat components including AP-2, Fcho1/2, Dab2, epsin 1, Hrb, Numb, stonin 2, synaptojanin 1, and ubiquitin. Residence of Eps15 at clathrin bud sites is not solely dependent on AP-2.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C30 present established knowledge about clathrin-mediated endocytosis and Eps15, appropriately supported by numerous citations. These claims provide the necessary background context for the study and are not novel findings but rather well-established facts from the literature.

results.result: The results confirm and extend previous data showing that ectopic expression of the tandem EH domain module can inhibit clathrin-mediated endocytosis and that removal of EH2+EH3 from EPS15 prevents proper targeting to clathrin-coated structures. Studies in Drosophila, squid, and yeast support the critical role of EH domains in Eps15 localization and function. The poor labeling of clathrin-coated structures with mNG-Nb E_142 indicates that the EH domain module is locally occupied at assembly zones and that any monomeric Nb E_142 bound to incoming EPS15/R is promptly displaced by the forming EH network. A plausible explanation for the apparent discrepancy between in vitro and in vivo binding is an increase in effective membrane concentration of endogenous EH binding partners at nascent clathrin bud sites by two-dimensional partitioning and avidity effects.
results.evaluation: Claims C172-C185 place the current findings in the context of previous work and provide mechanistic interpretation. The comparison to prior studies (C172-C179) is appropriately supported by citations, and the mechanistic interpretation about EH domain occupancy and avidity effects (C180-C185) is well-reasoned and consistent with the data.

results.result: The results from triple-null clone #40 cells expressing mitochondria-bound Nb E_142 illustrate that without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R, coated assemblies do not form stably and clathrin-mediated endocytosis falters. The steady-state perdurance of clathrin-coated structures depends on EPS15 presence in clone #40 cells, albeit with abnormal morphology. In parental HeLa cells, loss of either FCHO1/2 or EPS15/R alone does not abolish uptake, indicating compensation and extensive redundancy in the pioneer interaction web. The experiments reveal that pioneers localized to the perimeter of clathrin-coated structures are generally necessary for inception of new clathrin-coated buds. The diminished AP-2 puncta in clone #40 cells highlights the supportive role the FCHO1/2-EPS15/R partnership plays in stabilizing active AP-2 at the cell surface. The strongest evidence for this model is the unmistakable reconstitution of apparently normal AP-2 puncta in the presence of membrane-tethered FCHO1 linker domain in clone #40 cells. Under normal circumstances, membrane-attached FCHO1/2 interacts with incoming EPS15/R through the μHD, steering AP-2-bound EPS15 to relay the heterotetramer to FCHO1/2 for local access to the activating linker. The dysregulation of transferrin receptor internalization in Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- mice is reminiscent of the phenotype of HeLa clone #40 cells with Nb E_142-mediated sequestration of EPS15.
